title: Ancient Rome
description: Test your knowledge of the Roman Republic and Empire, from legendary founding to fall

questions.question: According to Roman tradition, in which year was the city of Rome founded?
questions.explanation: Roman tradition dated the founding of the city to 753 BC, the legendary date associated with Romulus. Historians treat it as legend, but Romans themselves counted years from it.

questions.question: Which river does the city of Rome stand on?
questions.explanation: Rome grew up on the banks of the Tiber, whose crossing point and access to the sea made the site valuable for trade.

questions.question: What were the three wars fought between Rome and Carthage called?
questions.explanation: The Punic Wars (264-146 BC) were fought between Rome and Carthage. The name comes from 'Punicus', the Latin word for Phoenician, the origin of Carthage's settlers.

questions.question: Which Carthaginian general famously crossed the Alps to invade Italy?
questions.explanation: Hannibal led an army, including war elephants, over the Alps into Italy during the Second Punic War. Scipio Africanus was the Roman general who ultimately defeated him.

questions.question: In which year was Julius Caesar assassinated?
questions.explanation: Caesar was assassinated in the Senate on the Ides of March (15 March) in 44 BC by a group of senators led by Brutus and Cassius.

questions.question: Who is considered the first Roman emperor?
questions.explanation: Augustus, born Octavian and the adopted heir of Julius Caesar, became the first emperor in 27 BC. Julius Caesar held the title of dictator but was never emperor.

questions.question: Which volcano erupted in AD 79 and buried the city of Pompeii?
questions.explanation: Mount Vesuvius erupted in AD 79, burying Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash and preserving much of both towns for archaeologists.

questions.question: What is the name of the great amphitheatre in Rome completed around AD 80?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum, also called the Flavian Amphitheatre, was completed under the emperor Titus and hosted gladiatorial games. The Circus Maximus was a chariot-racing track.

questions.question: Which emperor, together with Licinius, issued the Edict of Milan in AD 313 granting toleration to Christians?
questions.explanation: Constantine I and Licinius issued the Edict of Milan in AD 313, which ended official persecution and granted religious toleration across the empire.

questions.question: Which year is conventionally given for the fall of the Western Roman Empire?
questions.explanation: In AD 476 the last western emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was deposed by Odoacer. The Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire continued until AD 1453.
